section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yitzchak's sowing is the general service of Torah and mitzvos, which is the "light sown for the righteous" and brings blessing.
section.t: And one can explain this,
based on what the Tzemach Tzedek said in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"6,
that it is brought in the Midrash7
"Yitzchak came, he too shone, as it is said8
'Light is sown for the righteous,' and it is written 'And Yitzchak sowed.'"
That is, the sowing that Yitzchak sowed is the "light sown for the righteous."
And in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu9
it is brought on the verse "And Yitzchak sowed": "There is no sowing except charity, as it is said10
'Sow for yourselves for charity.'"
And it is explained in the maamar11,
that what is said in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu, that "And Yitzchak sowed" is charity, also applies to all the mitzvos, which are called by the name "charity,"
as it is said12
"And it shall be charity for us13."
And also the Torah is called by the name "sowing,"
as it is said14
"Six years you shall sow your field" — these are the six orders of the Mishnah15.
And this is that "And Yitzchak sowed" is the "light sown for the righteous,"
which is the light of Torah and mitzvos that is sown
(clothed)
in the physical things of this world16.
And based on this, one can explain that through the service of "vayizra" (and he sowed), "the man grew"
(in his entirety),
for "And Yitzchak sowed" is a general service,
the service of Torah study and fulfillment of mitzvos.
And based on this, one can say,
that also the two matters in the verse "And Yitzchak sowed etc."
("and he found a hundred measures,"
"and Hashem blessed him")
are general matters.
For just as the service of "vayizra Yitzchak" is a general service
(as above),
so too the matters drawn from above through this service are general matters.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the term "sowing" for Torah and mitzvos refers to a descent for the sake of ascent, and that man's service also involves sowing the intellect and emotions of the Nefesh HaElokis into the Nefesh HaBahamis.
section.t: And it is explained in many places17,
that this — that Torah and mitzvos are called by the name "sowing" — refers to the descent of Torah and mitzvos to clothe in physical things,
the intention of which is for the sake of ascent,
similar to sowing in the earth, which is for the sake of growth in greater multiplicity than was initially.
And one must understand,
that according to this explanation,
the term "sowing" regarding Torah and mitzvos applies with respect to the Holy One, blessed be He,
who brought down the Torah and mitzvos below18,
and not with respect to man's fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos.
From what is said "And Yitzchak sowed," it is understood that also man's fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is a descent for the sake of ascent.
And one can explain this based on what is said in the maamar at its end11
[regarding] another explanation of "light is sown for the righteous,"
that the matter of sowing is to sow into the animal soul the drawing down of the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul,
through which there is growth and ascent in the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul.
For since the root of the animal soul is above the root of the G-dly soul,
the root of the G-dly soul being in Tikkun (rectification) and the root of the animal soul being in Tohu (chaos),
therefore,
through the sowing of the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul into the animal soul, growth occurs
(ascent)
in the G-dly soul.
And to note,
in Likkutei Torah19
it is explained that "light is sown for the righteous" refers to the descent of the G-dly soul to clothe in the animal soul,
and from the language of the maamar — "to sow into the animal soul the drawing down of the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul" —
it implies,
that man must sow the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul into the animal soul.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of the soul involves two modes, and that to refine the animal soul, the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul must descend and clothe themselves in those of the animal soul, which is the meaning of "sowing" in man's fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos.
section.t: And the matter is,
that in the service of the soul
(even after its descent below)
there are two modes.
The service of the soul from its own side,
and its service to refine the animal soul20.
And this is the explanation of "to sow the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul into the animal soul,"
for the intellect and emotions of the G-dly soul as they are from their own side
(even after the descent of the soul below)
cannot, through them, effect the refinement of the animal soul,
and in order for them to act upon the animal soul, it is through their descent and clothing in the intellect and emotions of the animal soul20,
[which is] sowing.
And one can say,
that similarly it is with the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,
that in order for there to be vitality in the Torah and mitzvos, it is when the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is with love and fear21,
and in order that through the love and fear of the soul there be vitality in the action of the mitzvos, through which they will be "blossoming upward"22,
it is through their descent and clothing in the action
(of the mitzvah)23.
And this is that man's fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is called by the name "sowing,"
"And Yitzchak sowed."
